scenes.heading: Types of chemical reactions
scenes.sub: Spot the pattern, predict the products
scenes.say: Millions of reactions happen around us, but most fit a handful of patterns. Spot the pattern, and you can predict the products before you've even seen the reaction.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Clicking Lego together, or pulling it apart
scenes.science: Synthesis joins (A + B → AB); decomposition splits (AB → A + B)
scenes.breaks: Lego pieces stay the same, but in reactions bonds break and form, making new substances.
scenes.say: Think of Lego. Clicking pieces together is synthesis: sodium and chlorine join to make sodium chloride. Pulling a model apart is decomposition: heating limestone splits it into lime and carbon dioxide. And just like a tight Lego joint, most decompositions need energy put in.

scenes.heading: The dance moves
scenes.say: Think of the patterns as dance moves. Synthesis: two join into one. Decomposition: one splits apart. Displacement: one cuts in and steals a partner. Precipitation: two couples swap partners.

scenes.heading: Predict a displacement
scenes.question: Will magnesium react with silver nitrate solution? If so, write the equation.
lines: Mg is well above Ag, so yes
scenes.say: In displacement, a more reactive metal pushes a less reactive one out of its compound. Magnesium is well above silver in the reactivity series, so yes, it reacts. Magnesium nitrate forms, and silver comes out as a solid. Balance it with two silver nitrates and two silvers.

scenes.heading: Precipitation
points: Two solutions mix → an insoluble solid
scenes.say: In precipitation, two solutions mix and two ions pair up into a solid that won't dissolve. Remember SNAP: sodium, nitrate, ammonium and potassium compounds are always soluble, so they're never the precipitate. Silver nitrate and sodium chloride make a white precipitate of silver chloride.

scenes.heading: Combustion
points: Limited oxygen → CO and/or soot, + H₂O
scenes.say: Combustion is a fuel reacting fast with oxygen. With plenty of oxygen, a hydrocarbon makes carbon dioxide and water. With limited oxygen, you also get toxic carbon monoxide or soot. That's why gas heaters need good ventilation.

scenes.heading: Energy in, energy out
scenes.say: Exothermic means heat exits: the surroundings warm up, and delta H is negative. Endothermic means heat enters: the surroundings cool down, and delta H is positive. A spark to start doesn't make burning endothermic. It's strongly exothermic overall.
scenes.caption: Exothermic means heat EXits: the surroundings warm up, and ΔH is negative. Endothermic means heat ENters: the surroundings cool down, and ΔH is positive. A spark to start doesn't make burning endothermic. It's strongly exothermic overall.

points: Combustion: CO₂ + H₂O with full oxygen
Exo: heat exits; endo: heat enters
scenes.say: Quick recap. Synthesis joins, decomposition splits. A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one. SNAP compounds never precipitate. Exothermic releases heat; endothermic takes it in. Now try the practice questions!
